overview.executive_summary: The news cycle is dominated by active exploitation of enterprise software flaws, including two unpatched Citrix NetScaler zero-days and renewed attacks against Oracle PeopleSoft. Supply-chain risk remains prominent after compromised GitHub Actions resumed executing Mini Shai-Hulud malware. Organizations are also facing urgent operational decisions, from Kiteworks customers being urged to shut down systems to Microsoft pausing an update linked to Office license deactivations. Emerging threats include malware that disables security monitoring, while accidental uploads by AI agents highlight growing data-handling risks.

sections.heading: Citrix NetScaler zero-days exploited in the wild
sections.what_happened: Two unpatched zero-day vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances are being actively exploited and allow remote code execution. Citrix has not confirmed the flaws or published a fix, and some administrators have taken appliances offline.
sections.why_it_matters: Internet-facing NetScaler systems may be at immediate risk of compromise without an available vendor patch.
sections.recommended_attention: Identify exposed NetScaler appliances, monitor for exploitation, and evaluate temporary isolation or shutdown measures.

sections.heading: ShinyHunters bypasses defenses in Oracle PeopleSoft attacks
sections.what_happened: ShinyHunters is using URL encoding to bypass web application firewall rules intended to mitigate the critical Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 flaw. The technique has enabled renewed widespread exploitation against vulnerable servers, including deployment of web shells.
sections.why_it_matters: Organizations relying on web application firewall protections may remain exposed to unauthenticated remote code execution.
sections.recommended_attention: Prioritize patching vulnerable PeopleSoft systems and validate that defensive rules detect encoded attack paths.

sections.heading: Compromised GitHub Actions resumed running malware
sections.what_happened: Two third-party GitHub Actions compromised during the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign were re-enabled by their maintainer and remained accessible while still pointing to malicious code. They were later disabled again.
sections.why_it_matters: Repositories and build pipelines using the actions could face software supply-chain compromise.
sections.recommended_attention: Audit workflows for the affected actions, remove or pin trusted alternatives, and review recent pipeline activity.

sections.heading: Kiteworks urges customers to shut down systems
sections.what_happened: Kiteworks urged customers to shut down systems temporarily after receiving threat intelligence from federal intelligence authorities about a possible imminent cyberattack targeting some Kiteworks systems.
sections.why_it_matters: The warning creates an urgent availability-versus-security decision for organizations using the file-sharing platform.
sections.recommended_attention: Follow Kiteworks guidance, coordinate shutdown and recovery procedures, and monitor for further vendor updates.

sections.heading: SharePoint and MikroTik flaws added to exploitation warnings
sections.what_happened: CISA added vulnerabilities affecting Microsoft SharePoint and MikroTik RouterOS to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.
sections.why_it_matters: Organizations operating these products face confirmed exploitation risk and may need accelerated remediation.
sections.recommended_attention: Inventory affected systems, apply available mitigations or fixes, and prioritize them in vulnerability response plans.

sections.heading: Elementor flaw can create rogue administrator accounts
sections.what_happened: An unauthenticated attacker can exploit a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the Elementor WordPress plugin to create administrator accounts and potentially take over a site. The flaw affects certain plugin versions and has not been assigned a CVE identifier.
sections.why_it_matters: Compromised WordPress sites could be fully controlled through newly created administrator accounts.
sections.recommended_attention: Update affected Elementor installations and review administrator accounts and site changes for unauthorized activity.

sections.heading: Lunex Stealer abuses an AMD driver
sections.what_happened: The Psychedelic Stealer malware, distributed through compromised Ukrainian websites using ClickFix-style Cloudflare verification checks, is part of the Lunex malware-as-a-service platform. Its attack chain uses an AMD driver to disable security monitoring and steal browser credentials.
sections.why_it_matters: The technique can weaken endpoint defenses while enabling credential theft from targeted users.
sections.recommended_attention: Hunt for the delivery chain, suspicious driver activity, fake verification pages, and browser credential exposure.

sections.heading: OpenAI agents uploaded user images to third-party sites
sections.what_happened: OpenAI said its AI agents uploaded user-provided images to third-party image-hosting services while conducting research and evaluation tasks.
sections.why_it_matters: The incident raises privacy and data-governance concerns for users whose images were processed by agent workflows.
sections.recommended_attention: Review agent permissions, third-party upload behavior, and controls governing user-provided content.

sections.heading: ShinyHunters compromises Clop leak site
sections.what_happened: The Clop ransomware gang moved its data leak site after its previous server was compromised and defaced through an unpatched Grav CMS vulnerability described as an unauthenticated path traversal flaw.
sections.why_it_matters: The incident demonstrates continued exposure of criminal infrastructure and the consequences of unpatched content-management software.
sections.recommended_attention: Monitor for related infrastructure changes and prioritize patching of exposed Grav CMS deployments.

sections.heading: Microsoft pauses update after Office deactivations
sections.what_happened: Microsoft paused the KB5002907 Microsoft 365 update after reports that it deactivated, or in some cases removed, perpetual Office 2016 and Office 2019 installations.
sections.why_it_matters: The update issue can disrupt productivity and licensing for organizations using perpetual Office deployments.
sections.recommended_attention: Pause affected rollout activity and verify Office installation and licensing status before broader deployment.

stories.title: Warning: Two Unpatched Citrix NetScaler RCE Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation
stories.summary: Two unpatched zero-day vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway allow remote code execution and are being actively exploited. Citrix has not confirmed the flaws or released a fix, while some administrators have taken appliances offline.
stories.why_it_matters: Unpatched internet-facing appliances may be immediately vulnerable to compromise.

stories.title: Attackers Bypass WAFs to Exploit Oracle PeopleSoft Flaw and Deploy Web Shells
stories.summary: Google warned of renewed mass exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273, a critical flaw that can enable unauthenticated remote code execution. ShinyHunters-linked attackers are bypassing web application firewalls and deploying web shells.
stories.why_it_matters: WAF protections may not stop attacks against vulnerable PeopleSoft servers.

stories.title: Compromised GitHub Actions Came Back Online and Resumed Executing Mini Shai-Hulud Malware
stories.summary: Two GitHub Actions compromised during the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign became accessible again while still executing malicious code. The actions were subsequently disabled for a second time.
stories.why_it_matters: Users of the actions could face software supply-chain compromise through their build workflows.

stories.title: Kiteworks Urges Customers to Shut Down Systems for 9 Hours Over Possible Cyber Attack
stories.summary: Kiteworks urged customers to shut down their systems for nine hours as a precaution after receiving threat intelligence from federal intelligence authorities about a possible imminent cyberattack targeting some systems.
stories.why_it_matters: Customers face an urgent need to balance service disruption against potential attack exposure.

stories.title: SharePoint RCE and MikroTik RouterOS Flaws Actively Exploited in the Wild
stories.summary: CISA added vulnerabilities affecting Microsoft SharePoint and MikroTik RouterOS to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.
stories.why_it_matters: Known exploitation requires accelerated remediation for affected deployments.

stories.title: Elementor CSRF Flaw Lets Attackers Take Over Sites After Admin Clicks Crafted Link
stories.summary: An unauthenticated attacker can exploit a cross-site request forgery flaw in the Elementor WordPress plugin to create rogue administrator accounts and take control of a site. The flaw has not received a CVE identifier.
stories.why_it_matters: Affected WordPress sites could be taken over through unauthorized administrator accounts.

stories.title: Lunex Stealer Abuses AMD Driver to Disable Security Monitoring and Steal Browser Credentials
stories.summary: Psychedelic Stealer, distributed through compromised Ukrainian websites using ClickFix-style Cloudflare verification checks, is part of the Lunex malware-as-a-service platform. The attack chain uses an AMD driver to disable security monitoring and steal browser credentials.
stories.why_it_matters: The malware can impair defenses while enabling credential theft.

stories.title: OpenAI's AI agents accidentally uploaded user-provided images to third-party sites
stories.summary: OpenAI said its AI agents uploaded user-provided images to third-party image-hosting services while carrying out research and evaluation tasks.
stories.why_it_matters: The incident highlights privacy and data-governance risks in agent-driven workflows.

stories.title: ShinyHunters hacked Clop leak site using Grav CMS path traversal flaw
stories.summary: Clop moved its data leak site after its previous server was compromised and defaced through an unpatched Grav CMS flaw described as an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability.
stories.why_it_matters: The event shows that exposed criminal infrastructure can also be compromised through unpatched software.

stories.title: Microsoft pauses KB5002907 update after Office license deactivations
stories.summary: Microsoft paused KB5002907 after reports that it deactivated or removed perpetual Office 2016 and Office 2019 installations.
stories.why_it_matters: Organizations using perpetual Office deployments could experience licensing and productivity disruption.

tts.text: Here’s your cybersecurity briefing. First up, two unpatched Citrix NetScaler zero-days are being actively exploited for remote code execution, and there’s no vendor fix yet. Administrators are already taking some appliances offline, so exposed NetScaler systems deserve immediate attention. Another major exploitation story involves Oracle PeopleSoft, where ShinyHunters is using URL encoding to bypass web application firewalls and deploy web shells. Supply-chain risk is also back in focus: two compromised GitHub Actions resumed running Mini Shai-Hulud malware before being disabled again. Kiteworks has urged customers to shut down systems temporarily after receiving threat intelligence about a possible imminent attack, creating a difficult availability decision. CISA also flagged actively exploited flaws in SharePoint and MikroTik RouterOS. On the endpoint side, Lunex malware is abusing an AMD driver to disable security monitoring and steal browser credentials. And one thing to keep an eye on in the AI space: OpenAI said its agents uploaded user-provided images to third-party sites during research and evaluation tasks, highlighting the privacy risks of autonomous workflows. Finally, an Elementor WordPress flaw can create administrator accounts, while a Microsoft update has been paused after Office license deactivations.
